claude_code.supported_min_source: the .claude-plugin/marketplace.json schema this catalog ships has been stable since 2.0.0; the previous floor was never validated
claude_code.verification_method: Real direct CLI check this run — `claude --version` on the runner reports `2.1.263 (Claude Code)`, continuing the run of live-CLI validation since 2.1.257. `validated_against` and `latest_known` both advance from 2.1.259 to **2.1.263** together (no divergence). Covers the 2.1.260 → 2.1.263 delta. 2.1.263 is fix-only with no itemized changelog entries — reviewed, nothing to adopt. Three items from 2.1.260/2.1.261 are documented: **Claude apps gateway `userPluginMarketplacesEnabled`/`userPluginUploadsEnabled`** (2.1.260) — new `desktop` policy keys letting an admin block end users from adding their own marketplaces or uploading local plugins in Claude Desktop, noted in the managed-environments section; the **`@synced`-plugin/managed-`enabledPlugins` marketplace-clone-fallback fix** (2.1.261) — a cloud session could previously discard a plugin already synced from claude.ai when managed settings force-enabled it via `enabledPlugins`, then fall back to a marketplace clone that could itself fail, noted alongside the existing `@synced` coexistence documentation; and **`/reload-plugins` in headless sessions** (2.1.260) — now available to the Desktop app and SDK command lists, not just interactive terminals. Reviewed and not applicable, checked directly rather than assumed: `/skill-doctor` (2.1.261, a runtime loaded-skill-usage/pruning tool — a different problem from `make validate-skills`'s static frontmatter check, so it doesn't fold into that target); `bashOutputMaxChars`/`taskOutputMaxChars` and `--append-subagent-system-prompt-file` (2.1.261, no script here produces output near any default limit and no subagent system prompt is ever passed); the reverted 2.1.259 `Read()`-deny-rule-on-Bash-args change (2.1.260, this repo documents no `Read(...)`/`Edit(...)` permission-rule examples anywhere); the URL-typed-marketplace-stored-as-a-directory path-containment fix (2.1.260, this catalog is always added as the `Tamircohen28/tamirs-marketplace` `github` shorthand, never a raw URL-typed marketplace source); model switching staying blocked after a plugin hook load failure, and separately after an organization-managed plugin's marketplace failed to load (both 2.1.260, no hooks and no managed-org marketplace configured for this personal catalog); and the managed `skillOverrides`-alias / `Skill(name)`-deny-rule-on-nested-skill fixes (2.1.260, this catalog's own skill lives at the bare path `.agents/skills/run-plugins-catalog`, not behind a plugin-bundled `<dir>:name` alias). Everything else in 2.1.260/2.1.261/2.1.263 (`/diff` panel, `/cost` cache-miss cause, `/advisor` text form, `oidc.scope_on_refresh`, and a long run of terminal/Remote-Control/VSCode/Bedrock/Vertex/model-picker fixes) is host/session/UI-side with zero marketplace-manifest, plugin-source, or skill-loading surface. `claude plugin validate --strict --json .agents/skills` (piped through `scripts/report-skill-validation.py`) and a full `make validate` (regenerate + validate manifests, `make agent:check`; 3 plugins in sync, no drift) both passed clean against the live 2.1.263 CLI. Prior 2.1.252→2.1.259 verification still holds unchanged; see the install guide's per-version sections for that full history. Catalog install previously verified with `claude plugin marketplace add Tamircohen28/tamirs-marketplace` followed by `claude plugin install <name>@tamirs-marketplace`.

cursor.supported_min_source: Cursor documents no minimum version for plugins; the floor is the version actually validated rather than guessed. The previous 0.45.0 floor predates Cursor's plugin system entirely
cursor.verification_method: latest desktop build from official Cursor download links (3.18.9, 2026-08-30 stable) cross-checked against cursor.com/changelog (feature 3.11; date-only entries through 2026-09-02 Self-Hosted Machines / Team Pools / partner sandboxes / computer use); team-marketplace import is a Dashboard flow

codex.supported_min_source: earliest release this catalog has claimed .agents/plugins/marketplace.json support for
codex.verification_method: documentary revalidation by this repo's standing Codex method (official release notes plus catalog compatibility review; the Codex CLI is not installed on the review machine). Reviewed every openai/codex release from 0.148.0 through 0.153.4 for plugin/marketplace changes: #41208 (0.151.0) reports invalid project marketplaces without hiding valid plugins, #41953 (0.153.0) enforces a marketplace source policy for OpenAI-curated plugins only, and #42149/#42150 (0.153.0) upgrade Git marketplaces from merged configuration and add remote-marketplace support to the plugin CLI. None alter the portable Agent Plugin catalog shape, so .agents/plugins/marketplace.json remains discoverable unchanged; 0.153.0 widens how it can be consumed rather than narrowing it.

opencode.supported_min_source: oldest version on which `skills.paths` discovery of a catalog plugin's skills was verified with `opencode debug skill`
opencode.verification_method: `opencode --version` on the maintainer machine (reported 1.18.29); latest from registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai. OpenCode has no marketplace, so the catalog itself cannot be installed — skill discovery is verified directly with `opencode debug skill`, pointing `skills.paths` at this repo's `.agents/skills` and confirming `run-plugins-catalog` resolves to its `SKILL.md`

capability_gaps.marketplace: OpenCode has no plugin marketplace and no plugin manifest, so this catalog cannot be added as an install source. Each plugin repo is installed directly — clone it and point `skills.paths` at its `skills/` directory, or symlink it into the OpenCode skills directory. Every plugin in this catalog ships its own `opencode.json` and its own OpenCode install guide.
capability_gaps.catalog_discovery: There is no OpenCode equivalent of listing plugins from a remote catalog. The plugin table in this repo's README is the discovery surface; installation is then per-repo.
